newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed in thin, random trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed in thin, random trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks continued their mixed, directionless trend in slow dealings enlivened only by a 3.5 billion peso cross deal between Corporacion Financiera del Valle (Corfivalle) shareholders.

Bogota's IBB index closed 0.17 percent higher at 864.56 in a trading volume of 4.1 billion pesos. Medellin's IBOMED general price index ended the session 0.29 percent off at 13.527.59 in thin trade of 644.3 million pesos.
About 470,000 Corfivalle common shares changed hands on the Bogota exchange with prices dropping 0.67 percent to 7,350 pesos each.

"If we take the Corfivalle cross deal out of the equation, we can see that markets were very sluggish, given that there are no buyers the size of foreign funds that are prepared to move until there's a real fall in interest rates," one Bogota broker said.
He added that the deal had been agreed between two of the corporation's shareholders and that the drop in price was not due to market conditions but to the nature of the deal.
Another major feature of the day's trading in Bogota was a 222 million peso cross deal on Banco Anglo Colombiano shares at a stable price of 64.5 pesos.

The IBB index was nudged up by a 4.18 percent rise in Banco de Bogot shares to 5,850 pesos on volume of 54.2 million pesos and a 0.56 percent rise in cement maker Cementos Argos to 5,350 pesos on a total trade of 81.8 million pesos.
"There were a number of deals and a small amount of profit-taking but we do not see any long-term trend developing in the markets," a trader on the Bogot exchange said.
The day's main mover in Medelln was a profit-take on paper and card manufacturer Cartn Colombia. Its share price closed down 2.63 percent at 1,850 pesos on a trade of 259.9 million pesos.

Of stocks traded in Medelln, just three posted gains, seven fell and nine remained unchanged. Gains were led by food manufacturer Industrias Alimenticias Noel, which rose 3.64 percent to 2,850, and by gas distributor Promigas which ended up 2.81 percent at 3,290.

Banco Industrial Colombiano saw 1.18 percent shaved off preferential shares on profit-taking, ending at 4,200 pesos on trade of 3.9 million pesos. Banco Ganadero closed 0.72 percent down at 277 on 3.6 million pesos trade.
